name: Entity
desc: Base class for entity relative movement and rotation updates. Subclasses S15 (rel move), S16 (look), S17 (move+look).

subclasses.name: S17PacketEntityLookMove
subclasses.desc: Both relative move and rotation update.

notes: S14 is the abstract base — the actual packet IDs are 0x15 (S15), 0x16 (S16), 0x17 (S17). All share the same class hierarchy. The client adds the relative deltas to the entity's current server position to get the new position.

writeup.p: S14PacketEntity is the abstract base for the three relative entity-movement packets. The wire IDs are S15PacketEntityRelMove (0x15), S16PacketEntityLook (0x16) and S17PacketEntityLookMove (0x17); the base class itself is never registered as a sendable ID and EnumConnectionState registers only the subclasses. Every variant carries a VarInt entityId and an onGround flag, plus byte deltas (x 32) and/or rotation bytes (x 256/360). The client accumulates the deltas onto the entity's last server position, so a position error in one tick carries into every later tick until the server sends an absolute S18.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleEntityMovement (Memeware 7.3 bundle, line 551) is shared by all three subclasses: it adds the packet's posX/posY/posZ to entity.serverPosX/Y/Z, recomputes the position as serverPos / 32.0, keeps the current yaw/pitch unless the packet carries rotation (S16/S17), then calls setPositionAndRotation2 with interpolation factor 3 and teleport flag false, and finally writes packetIn.onGround into entity.onGround. Server-side, EntityTrackerEntry picks the variant by motion magnitude: look-move when both position and rotation changed, rel-move when only position changed, look when only rotation changed (corpus lines 213-217, 265).

The 8-client corpus shows three consumer families, none of them ESP. Rise 6.x combat: LegitReach accumulates a server-truth realPosition from S14 deltas for its ping-spoof reach, and WatchdogVelocity buffers the S15/S16/S17 subclasses and replays them for its Watchdog Backtrack mode. Rise 6.x infrastructure: the translation component's PacketType enum maps ENTITY_REL_MOVE, ENTITY_LOOK_MOVE and ENTITY_LOOK into a per-entity position cache, and PingSpoofComponent classifies all S14 subclasses in its players tuple. Rise 5.99 anticheat: PlayerData re-derives position, deltas and onGround from S15/S17 and feeds KeepSprintA, SpeedA, EagleA and GroundSpoofA/B. Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy and Tenacity reference the packet only through the vanilla handler. LiquidSense Dev consumes the stream for bot detection: AntiBot records per-entity ground/air/invaildGround flags from the S14 onGround bit, and its MixinNetHandlerPlayClient fires an EntityMovementEvent from handleEntityMovement for modules that react to entity movement. November Recode 2.0 has no S14 corpus hit; it processes the packet through the vanilla handler only.

Relative deltas are trusted per packet and corrected only by S18, which makes the S14 stream the raw material of every position-based client-side simulation: reach modules reconstruct the opponent's true position, anticheats reconstruct it to verify onGround transitions and speed. The onGround bit is authoritative for the tick it arrives in, which is exactly what GroundSpoofA/B and EagleA test. Reach exploits work through latency: LegitReach delays all player-class packets so the server keeps a stale player position while the client attacks from a closer interpolated one. Dropping or reordering S14 packets is invisible to the server because they are clientbound state announcements with no acknowledgement.

implementation.overview: The relative movement family (S15/S16/S17 under the S14 base) is the highest-frequency entity state in the play state. In the 8 clients it feeds three things: Rise 6.x reach and backtrack modules that rebuild a server-truth position, Rise 6.x packet-classification components, and the Rise 5.99 built-in anticheat that replays server-side style checks against the reconstructed position stream. LiquidSense Dev's AntiBot reads the same stream to classify bots by onGround transitions.
implementation.server_handling: The server never processes S14 on receive; it is purely clientbound. The client handler accumulates: entity.serverPosX += posX (and Y/Z), position = serverPos / 32.0, rotation kept unless S16/S17 carry bytes, then setPositionAndRotation2(..., 3, false) and entity.onGround = packet onGround. Because the accumulation never resets, any dropped packet permanently shifts the entity by its delta until an S18 arrives. EntityTrackerEntry emits S15/S16/S17 at the tracking update rate (every 2 ticks for players, more often for fast entities) and switches to S18 once the one-tick displacement exceeds the 4-block threshold.
implementation.protocol_notes: Deltas are signed bytes x 32, so a single packet moves an entity at most 3.97 blocks per axis; rotation bytes decode as yaw * 360 / 256. The onGround flag is present on the base class and therefore on all three subclasses. S16 (look) and S17 (look-move) are the only places the body yaw/pitch of a tracked entity changes; S19PacketEntityHeadLook separately updates only the head yaw. There is no ordering guarantee between S14 and S18 for the same entity; a teleport supersedes any pending deltas because it overwrites serverPosX/Y/Z.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Client-side anticheats (Rise 5.99) and server anticheats both treat the S14 stream as ground truth for movement verification. Ground-spoof detection keys on the onGround flag combined with block probes; eagle detection on the sneak flag in the S1C metadata stream timed against S14 ticks; keepsprint on the speed delta around S0B animations. For cheat clients, the S14 stream is what makes ping-spoof reach and backtrack possible: buffering it has zero server cost, and the server cannot distinguish a delayed entity stream from lag. The trade-off is visual, not statistical: held entity packets produce stutter and frozen-head artifacts that staff can spot.

modules.name: LegitReach
modules.purpose: Extend effective attack range by ping-spoofing the server's view of the player while the opponent's real position is tracked from the S14/S18 stream.
modules.how_it_works: On PostMotionEvent it picks the nearest target (TargetComponent.getTargets(9)). realPosition is seeded from the entity's client position and then maintained on PacketReceiveEvent: S14 deltas are added via getPosX() / 32D, S18 snaps it to absolute coordinates. When realDistance exceeds clientDistance and lands inside 2.3-5.9 blocks, it calls PingSpoofComponent.spoof(maxPingSpoof, true, true, true, true) so all incoming player-class packets are parked for up to the configured milliseconds; otherwise it disables and dispatches the component. Render3DEvent draws the real-location bounding box with eased animation.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The server never sees the S14 packets (clientbound), so the exploit is purely about the server's measured player position going stale. Servers that timestamp hits against the latest player position defeat it; Watchdog-style anticheats that confirm position before damage registration flag the hit timing.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 ships the identical module (same package and class); the only difference is the corpus path (com/alan/clients/... without the Client-release2 prefix).

modules.name: WatchdogVelocity
modules.purpose: Velocity cancel combined with an entity backtrack: the S14 subclasses are held and replayed to keep the client and server entity timelines deliberately divergent.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketReceiveEvent, S12 velocity for self is cancelled (with a stacking option), C0F/C00 are held while active, and with Watchdog Backtrack enabled the three S14 subclasses plus S19PacketEntityHeadLook and S18PacketEntityTeleport are cancelled and queued. The queue is replayed through PacketUtil.receive after 100-250 ms, when the distance to the tracked realPosition crosses the 4.5/2.5 thresholds, when the player takes damage (hurtTime == 9), or during the first 100 ticks of a world. realPosition is accumulated from S14 and re-anchored by S18.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketReceiveEvent, JumpEvent, PreUpdateEvent, StrafeEvent, PostStrafeEvent, Render3DEvent.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Buffering clientbound packets is invisible to the server, so the backtrack itself never flags. The velocity-cancel half is the detectable part: a missing motionY after a confirmed hurt status is the classic flag, which is why the module gates cancellation on offGroundTicks, water and scaffold state.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 does not reference the S14 subclasses in its WatchdogVelocity (the corpus hit is 6.2.4 only).

modules.name: KeepSprintA / GroundSpoofA (Rise anticheat)
modules.purpose: Client-side reproductions of server anticheat checks; the S14 stream is their movement clock and position source.
modules.how_it_works: PlayerData.handle converts S15/S17 deltas into per-tick position, deltas and onGround (block probes at y - 0.43 and y - 0.99). KeepSprintA times S0B arm swings against S14 ticks, samples horizontal speed into attackingSamples vs beforeAttackingSamples and fails when the attack-period average exceeds the baseline by more than 0.15 while on ground. GroundSpoofA/B and SpeedA consume the same reconstructed state. EagleA is documented under S1CPacketEntityMetadata because it needs the sneak flag from the metadata stream.
modules.vanilla_hook: Raw packet stream via PlayerData.handle (no event bus); S14, S18, S12, S0B.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: This is Rise's own anticheat for serverside-style protection of its users; the S14-derived position is rebuilt exactly as a server would, so the checks inherit the server's blind spots (they only see what the server sent, which is all the server knows).
modules.variations: SpeedA, EagleA and GroundSpoofA/B are separate checks over the same PlayerData; PacketUtil.isRelMove / isLookMove in dev/rise/anticheat/util/PacketUtil classify the subclasses.

modules.name: PacketType (translation component)
modules.purpose: Maintain a per-entity position cache that mirrors server state independently of the vanilla interpolation, fed by the S14 subclasses, S18, S19 and spawn packets.
modules.how_it_works: An enum of packet classes with a BiFunction per entry: ENTITY_REL_MOVE adds deltas to the cached Position, ENTITY_LOOK_MOVE and ENTITY_LOOK replace yaw/pitch (returning null when no entry exists), ENTITY_TELEPORT sets the entry to absolute coordinates, DESTROY_ENTITY removes it, and ENTITY_HEAD_LOOK writes the decoded head yaw into the yaw slot. Decoding is / 32.0 for position and * 360 / 256 for angles.
modules.vanilla_hook: Invoked from the translation component's packet receive path.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Pure client-side bookkeeping with no server interaction. The look-only handlers returning null for unknown entities means the cache silently drops rotations until a spawn packet seeds it, a quirk downstream aim code must tolerate.
modules.variations: Identical in Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4; the corpus path differs only by the Client-release2/Client/src/main/java prefix.

modules.name: AntiBot (movement tracking)
modules.purpose: Classify anti-cheat bots by their S14 movement stream: which entities ever touch ground, fly in air, or move while reporting onGround.
modules.how_it_works: onPacket fires for every S14PacketEntity: if the entity is a player, record the entity id in the ground/air lists by the onGround bit, and count in invaildGround every onGround packet where prevPosY != posY (halved on air packets). isBot() consumes the lists: groundValue flags entities never seen on ground, airValue flags never-seen-in-air, invaildGroundValue flags a count >= 10, plus the usual name/tab/derp checks.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketEvent (receive), UpdateEvent for the removal loop, AttackEvent for hit tracking.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The bot checks feed isBot(), which per the module description KillAura consults before targeting; the movement-derived heuristics (never grounded, invalid ground) are signature based and only as good as the S14 stream the server sends.
modules.variations: The invaildGround counter treats onGround with a y change as suspicious, a heuristic aimed at teleporting bots; no other corpus client derives bot state from S14.

implementation.general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent in Rise 6.x for modules; the Rise 5.99 anticheat receives every packet through PlayerData.handle instead of an event bus. LiquidSense Dev re-dispatches S14 as an EntityMovementEvent from its handleEntityMovement mixin on NetHandlerPlayClient; its AntiBot reads the raw packet on the client PacketEvent.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 anticheat decodes S14 via MCP-style accessors (func_149062_c, func_149060_h); Rise 6.x uses getPosX/getYaw accessors, and WatchdogVelocity switches on the packet class with Java 17 pattern matching while LegitReach and PacketType use instanceof chains. Deltas are consistently divided by 32.0 and angles multiplied by 360/256 across every client. November Recode 2.0 has no S14 corpus hit. LiquidSense Dev reads S14 in AntiBot and re-dispatches it as EntityMovementEvent from the NetHandlerPlayClient mixin.

anticheat.overview: Server-side anticheats never see S14 on the wire: it is a clientbound announcement of entity relative movement, rotation and ground state. What they do see is the same stream on the send side, and the richest anticheats use it to keep a lag-compensated copy of every tracked entity's position so reach, phase and velocity checks compare the player against where the server actually believes entities are. The corpus splits into position-replication trackers (Hydro, Kauri, AntiHaxerman), wrappers that classify the S14 subclasses into a packet pipeline (Frequency, Artemis, FlopAC), and reach checks that either consume the replicated positions or, in ThotPatrol's case, admit that rel-move plus AABB would beat their own Bukkit-based math.

checks.name: TrackedEntity (entity position replication)
checks.purpose: Rebuild other entities' positions from the S14 relative-move stream so reach and aim checks can query server-truth entity locations instead of trusting the player's rendered view.
checks.how_it_works: handleMovement(deltaX, deltaY, deltaZ) wraps the S14 byte deltas into an EntityMovement of type RELATIVE, marks the entity as awaiting confirmation, and applies the deltas to every TrackedPosition in the queue. handlePostFlying advances the queue when the player's next flying packet confirms the tick, and handlePostTransaction removes positions that the confirmed state has passed. Confirmed and pending positions are exposed separately (getX/getY/getZ versus getPendingPosition), so checks can evaluate both the server-known location and the one the client has just been told about.
checks.detects: Position desync between the server's entity stream and the client's render state, and provides the entity location used to verify reach against delayed or interpolated entity positions.
checks.variations: Hydro's EntityTracker drives this class from PacketSendEvent, applying the deltas inside the transaction tracker's confirm window. AntiHaxerman's EntityTracker accumulates the same deltas into serverPosX/Y/Z and divides by 32.0 on connection confirm; Kauri's EntityTrackHandler adds the deltas into an interpolating EntityLocation with transaction-anchored application.

checks.name: EntityTrackHandler (entity move tracking)
checks.purpose: Keep a server-side copy of every tracked entity's interpolated location from the S14 stream, and spawn fake mobs around a target to verify that the client's own entity tracking and aim match the server's.
checks.how_it_works: onRelPosition looks up the entity in the world tracker, skips non-allowed types, then adds the packet's x, y, z, yaw and pitch to the entity's new EntityLocation and sets the interpolation increment to 3. onFlying advances interpolation for every tracked entity whenever the player sends a flying packet. runAction delays the state change until a transaction confirms, or uses an instant action for the current combat target, timestamping entity updates against the player's connection. For a teleporting target it spawns three magma-cube fake mobs around the entity plus a slime on the player's aim ray, then moves them with the entity, so the client's hitbox testing can be verified server-side.
checks.detects: Killaura that attacks where the server holds no entity, hitbox spoofing, and clients whose entity tracking diverges from the sent stream.
checks.variations: The same handler applies S18 teleports through onTeleportSent and S20 attributes through updateAttributes; WPacketPlayOutEntity is Kauri's internal wrapper for the S14 subclasses. Hydro and AntiHaxerman cover the same tracking duty with simpler, non-interpolating position queues.

checks.name: ReachD (reach against player positions)
checks.purpose: Classic 1.8 reach check; the corpus hit is the author's own TODO comment stating that tracking PacketPlayOutRelEntityMove and testing the AABB would be far more accurate than the Bukkit-position math the check actually uses.
checks.how_it_works: On PacketAttackEvent the check measures the distance between attacker and victim eye locations, subtracts the vertical difference and a fixed 0.32 hitbox accommodation, and compares the result against maxReach. The threshold is inflated by ground state, yaw difference, recent horizontal speed (tracked on PlayerMoveEvent), the average ping of both players, TPS and the attacker's speed potion level. Three consecutive exceedances log a cheat.
checks.detects: Blatant reach abuse against players, with tolerance for lag, elevation and speed.
checks.variations: The commented TODO names the S14-based approach (accumulating rel-move deltas and testing the entity AABB) as the accurate alternative; the modern trackers in this corpus (Hydro TrackedEntity, Kauri EntityTrackHandler, AntiHaxerman EntityTracker) implement exactly that approach and feed it into their own reach checks.

checks.name: NetworkFilter (entity packet admission control)
checks.purpose: Whitelist the packet classes AntiHaxerman's trackers may consume, including the three S14 subclasses, so entity replication only runs for state that actually reaches the client.
checks.how_it_works: The constructor registers GPacketPlayServerEntity and its Look, RelEntityMove and RelEntityMoveLook inner classes, plus entity teleport, spawn, destroy, velocity, attributes and the movement/transaction set. isAllowed is the gate every later pipeline stage checks before processing a packet.
checks.detects: Nothing directly; it is admission control for the tracker pipeline that feeds reach, velocity and position checks.
checks.variations: Artemis reaches the same packet family through GPacketPlayServerEntity, Frequency through WrappedPacketPlayOutEntity, and FlopAC through its tinyprotocol NMSObject/Packet layer; all three appear in the corpus for the same reason.

checks.name: WrappedPacketPlayOutEntity (S14 wrapper)
checks.purpose: Minimal 1.8 wrapper exposing the S14 base packet to Frequency's outgoing packet pipeline.
checks.how_it_works: The class extends PacketWrapper over PacketPlayOutEntity, giving the processor layer a typed handle for entity move packets. The identical file ships in the FrequencyPlus fork and in Degrade, which is a Frequency derivative.
checks.detects: Nothing directly; infrastructure for the processor pipeline that classifies entity packets.
checks.variations: FrequencyPlus (MinecraftUserHAN1110) and Degrade (splatboydev) carry byte-identical copies of the file. AutoEye's PacketPlayOutEntity wrapper and FlopAC's tinyprotocol layer serve the same role on their own bases.
